title: Render side-by-side look captures for the CEO to pick from
tier_reason: Rendering captures and bringing them into chat changes nothing players see; the pick itself comes back to Daniel.
ask: Get the look session captures rendered so I can pick a look.
first_action: Ask Ingrid to name the treatments worth showing, then have Jade render one capture per treatment from the real game on the same farm, time of day, and seed.
source_message: Yes - go ahead and get the look session captures rendered for me first, and tell Dmitri to hold the foley session until I've picked a look.
result:
Here's where the look session actually stands, and the one thing that blocks the renders.

**The treatments worth showing** (my strawman for Ingrid to confirm — she owns the final list):

1. **As it ships today** — the control. Everything else gets judged against it.
2. **Warmer cozy** — same sprites, richer saturation and deeper hue-shifted shadows. The style guide's rules turned up.
3. **Cooler, quieter world** — ambient pulled toward grey-green and desaturated, so the only saturated pixels on screen are the things you can touch. This is the one that leaves the near-future door open.
4. **More fidelity** — more shading steps per material, softer edges. This is the only one that can't be faked; it needs sheets actually regenerated.

**Staging, identical across all four:** the field mid-morning on day three, seed 12345 (what the visual-regression rig already uses), crops at mixed growth, the player and one station in frame, same camera, same frame number.

**The blocker.** Treatments 1–3 are a recolor of one captured frame — free, reversible, an hour of work. Treatment 4 costs real money at the image pipeline, so it needs your yes before Yuki generates anything. And I couldn't launch the game from this session — running Godot here got declined, so the capture itself has to happen in a build session on the desktop.

**Owners:** Ingrid confirms or edits the four. Jade captures the base frame and produces 1–3. Yuki does 4 if you approve the spend. I'll bring all of them back here side by side with a plain-language quiz.

One question worth answering now: do you want treatment 4 in the lineup? Without it the session can only tell you about color, not about how detailed the game should look — and "how far from the current look" is half of what you're picking.
